subject: problems populating matrix with numbers in shiny... code works on the R console, but not in shiny

messages.author: b505db3b5deef952
messages.subject: problems populating matrix with numbers in shiny... code works on the R console, but not in shiny
parts:
Dear shiny Users,
I have run into a wall with some bugs that I can not seem to fix. I am trying to create an interactive shiny app that will run some simulations of allele frequency over time (generations) with user input of population size etc, the results of which are then graphed with ggplot2. 

The Code works just fine when entered in the R console (simulations produced and graphed), but when I try to implement it in shiny it gives me some strange errors. The ui.R file has no issues and the side panel populates as expected (code not shown). 

The error is in the server.R file. The error I keep getting is :

Error in X[i, j] = q.i^2 ...

 number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length

I think the problem is in how the matrix or array is being populated through the loop I've set up. Basically, I created an array with 0's and only the first row has an initial value. Then the code loops over columns and rows and calculates the frequency of the allele in each generation (row) for each simulation (column).

Code below. Highlighted in red is the line that seems to be tripping up the code and causing the error "number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length". 



library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  
  
  output$plot <- reactivePlot(function() {
    
    q = 1 - (as.numeric(input$p))
    N.chrom = 2*as.numeric(input$N)
   
    
    X = array(0, dim=c(1000,200))
    X[1,] = rep(.5,200) # initialize frequency of A1 alleles in first generation
    for(j in 1:200){
      for(i in 2:1000){
        q.i = rbinom(1,N.chrom,prob=X[i-1,j])/N.chrom
        meanfit <-(1-q.i)^2*as.numeric(input$wAA)+2*(1-q.i)*q.i*as.numeric(input$wAB)+q.i^2*as.numeric(input$wBB)
        X[i,j] = q.i^2*as.numeric(input$wBB)/meanfit + q.i*(1-q.i)*as.numeric(input$wAB)/meanfit
      } 
    }
    
    X = data.frame(X)
    
    sim_data <- melt(X)
    
    p <- ggplot(sim_data, aes(x = rep(c(1:ngens), nsims), y = value, colour = variable)) + geom_line()
    
    
    print(p)
    
  }, height=700)
  
})

I had a hunch that something was going on as I was getting errors just trying to rep the initial value in the first row of the array. Originally I wanted to take user input to specify the number of simulations (nsims), and thus reps (columns)  from the ui.R script. 

X = array(0, dim=c(1000,200))
X[1,] = rep(q,nsims) # initialize frequency of A1 alleles in first generation                                                                      

Error in X[1, ] = rep(1 - q, nsims) : 
  number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length


I got around that error when I replaced nsims (which is taken from user input) with a number (200), which is how I have it in the server.R script above.  


Is there something major that I am missing about how shiny handles variables or fills arrays or vectors? The replacement length errors do not make sense to me as the array has the same dimensions as the numbers I am looping over (200 columns, 1000 rows). Again this code runs fine on R. 

Any help or advice would me much appreciated. I imagine this is something simple, but I can't seem to get ahead of it. 

Thanks,
LP
